about.heading: Is your HTTPS ready for quantum computers?
about.intro: One scan. Four checks. One grade from A+ to F. Free and open source.

checks.title: TLS versions
checks.body: TLS 1.0 to 1.3. Old versions get flagged.

checks.title: Post-quantum ML-KEM
checks.body: Does your server speak X25519MLKEM768? Find out in seconds.

checks.title: SSL certificate
checks.body: Issuer, expiry, key strength, trust. Expiring soon? You'll know.

checks.title: Security headers
checks.body: HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options. Protected, weak or missing.

faq.a: Encryption quantum computers can't break. The standard is X25519MLKEM768: classic X25519 plus ML-KEM-768 (NIST FIPS 203).
Attackers save encrypted traffic today and crack it when quantum computers arrive. Chrome, Firefox and Cloudflare already use ML-KEM. Your server should too.
No. Dead since 2021 (RFC 8996). Turn them off, or your grade stops at B.
HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options. Missing or weak? QScan shows you.

faq.q: How do I get an A+?
faq.a: TLS 1.3, no old TLS, a valid certificate, strong HSTS and all four headers in place. ML-KEM earns a bonus. A bad certificate is an instant F.

faq.q: Is it safe? Is anything stored?
faq.a: Yes, it's safe: a scan looks like a normal visit. Nothing is stored. Only scan sites you own or may test.

footer.note: Public sites only. Results reflect the moment of the scan.
